parsed.office_action: SUMMARY The Office has considered the applicant’s January 25, 2010 amendment and remarks (documents G5146XBDPPOPPY5, G5146XGHPPOPPY5, G5146XGWPPOPPY5, G5146XHSPPOPPY5, G5146XIGPPOPPY5 and G5146XITPPOPPY5). The amendment cancels claims 3, 5, 8 and 10 and presents amended independent claims 1 and 6 and dependent claims 2, 4, 7 and 9. The prior Non-Final Office action of October 29, 2009 (document G1DP23M1PPOPPY5) relied upon US 2005/0083307 (Aufderheide) for rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103. After review, the Examiner finds the amendment and applicant’s remarks do not overcome the cited rejections for the reasons below. Rejections maintained (summary): - Claims 1, 4, 6 and 9 — Rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as anticipated by Aufderheide (US 2005/0083307). - Claims 2 and 7 — Rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as unpatentable over Aufderheide. Canceled claims: 3, 5, 8 and 10 have been canceled by applicant and are not considered further. ANALYSIS OF THE AMENDMENT AND REMARKS 1) Anticipation (35 U.S.C. 102) — claims 1, 4, 6, 9 Applicant amended the independent claims to add that the carbon layer “is arranged to overlay said printed silver conductor layer or said insulation layer for avoiding dissociation of silver ions from said printed silver layer.” The Office previously explained and the record supports that Aufderheide discloses multilayer resistive touch constructions with ITO conductive films, printed silver conductors and carbon conductive inks, as well as insulating and adhesive layers. The prior action notes and applicant’s own remarks draw attention to Aufderheide’s teaching that carbon conductive ink can be printed over silver ink “on the end of the tail to protect the traces from corrosion and abrasion” (see the record citation). That teaching shows application of carbon over silver for protection — the same arrangement recited in the amended independent claims. The newly added language is a general functional statement (preventing silver dissociation) and does not identify a structural limitation or a specific arrangement that is absent from Aufderheide. Consequently, the elements as amended remain disclosed or enabled by Aufderheide and the anticipation rejection is maintained for the recited claims. 2) Obviousness (35 U.S.C. 103) — claims 2 and 7 Claims 2 and 7 further limit the layer order (printed silver on ITO; carbon overlaid on printed silver; insulation overlaid the carbon layer; adhesive overlaid the insulation layer, etc.). Aufderheide describes ITO conductive films, application of silver conductors thereon, use of solvent-based epoxy insulating inks, and screen-printing carbon conductive ink over silver traces to protect them. Given these teachings, arranging the listed materials in the claimed order for corrosion protection and device fabrication would have been within the routine skill of one of ordinary skill in the art. Applicant’s remarks point to distinctions based on “operated zones” vs. “non-operated zones” and the alleged limitation that Aufderheide’s carbon printing is limited to trace tail ends. Those arguments are noted but are not supported by record evidence showing a technical distinction or unexpected result that would overcome obviousness. Therefore, the 103 rejections for claims 2 and 7 are maintained. 3) Applicant’s arguments about distinctions and amendments Applicant argues that the claimed carbon arrangement is for non-operated zones and that Aufderheide’s carbon teaching pertains only to tail ends for protection. The record shows Aufderheide expressly contemplates printing carbon conductive ink over silver ink traces where corrosion protection is required (paragraph [0048]), and teaches suitable substrates (plastic or glass) and insulating/adhesive materials. Applicant has not submitted factual evidence (e.g., comparative data, expert declaration, or persuasive claim construction showing the claimed “non-operated zones” limitation excludes Aufderheide’s disclosure) to overcome the rejections. 4) Drawings/Abstract/Specification corrections Applicant submitted corrected text for paragraph [0020], an amended abstract, and replacement drawing sheets (remarks indicate Figures 9-11 bracket removal and correction of electrode numbering in the specification). The corrections to the specification and abstract respond to the earlier objections; the drawing objection under 37 C.F.R. 1.84(p)(5) and 1.84(p)(1) is considered in light of the submitted replacement drawing sheets. If the drawing replacement sheets fully correct the earlier identified deficiencies, the drawing objections will be withdrawn. If the Examiner identifies discrepancies upon formal review of the replacement sheets, a subsequent Office action will notify applicant. (Note: review of the replacement drawings on file is in progress; any remaining formal drawing defects will be raised in a subsequent communication.) 5) Priority documents Applicant previously asserted foreign priority (Taiwanese application filed January 17, 2007). The record contains a note that a certified copy of the foreign priority application has not been filed as required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b). If priority is to be relied upon, applicant should submit the certified copy as required. OPTIONS TO ADVANCE PROSECUTION To overcome the maintained rejections applicant may consider one or more of the following: - Amend the claims to recite specific, limiting structural or process features that are not taught or suggested by Aufderheide (for example, limited geometry, placement, manufacturing steps, compositions, thicknesses, or a functional limitation tied to a structural feature that yields an unexpected technical advantage). Broad functional language that reads on the same protection use taught in Aufderheide will not distinguish the claims. - Provide persuasive evidence and explanation (e.g., declaration under 37 C.F.R. 1.132, comparative data) that the claimed arrangement achieves an unexpected result or a technical advantage not taught or suggested by Aufderheide. Evidence should establish facts not apparent from the prior art itself. - Argue claim construction and point to explicit, supported distinctions in the specification and drawings that tie the claimed subject matter to features absent from Aufderheide. Present clear record citations if relying on the specification to interpret claim terms. - If applicant contends Aufderheide’s disclosure is nonanalogous or does not teach the claimed elements, point to the specific passages in Aufderheide (with copies or highlighted citations) and provide a legal and factual explanation why those teachings do not anticipate or render obvious the claimed subject matter. NEXT ACTION Applicant is given ONE MONTH from the mailing date of this communication to reply with amendments and/or arguments and/or evidence. Absent a persuasive reply that overcomes the cited rejections, the Examiner will issue a further Office action (which may be final) addressing any remaining claims and issues. The applicant should also ensure submission of the certified foreign priority document if priority is to be maintained. Limitations: this communication relies on the record documents available through the A1 date. The Examiner’s citations to Aufderheide are based on the Office action in the record (document G1DP23M1PPOPPY5). If applicant submits new evidence or claim changes not yet in the record, the Examiner will consider them upon timely reply.

parsed.office_action:
Response to Applicant's After-Final/Amendment Filing (A1) — Non-Final Examiner Action
Summary of status
- Applicant's A1 filing (dated 2011-11-29, doc GVNXDYBTPXXIFW1) cancels claims 1–13 and submits an amendment to claim 14. The cancellations are entered and those cancelled claims are no longer before the Office. (GVNXDYBTPXXIFW1: "1 to 13 (Cancelled).")
- Corrected formal drawings were submitted on 2011-12-13 (GW5F0MGKPXXIFW3). The drawing objections in the August 1, 2011 Office action are considered addressed by the corrected replacement sheet and the drawing objections are therefore withdrawn.
- The Examiner has reviewed the amended claim 14 and the arguments presented in the Applicant's Remarks. The Examiner maintains the prior rejection of claim 14 under 35 U.S.C. 103 for the reasons set forth below, but notes a formal objection that the amended claim text contains a typographical/formatting error that must be corrected.
Claim-level disposition and reasoning
1) Claims 1–13
Status: Withdrawn from prosecution (cancelled by applicant).
Evidence: Applicant's A1 (GVNXDYBTPXXIFW1) expressly states "1 to 13 (Cancelled)." As cancelled claims, any rejections previously asserted against those claims are terminated as to them.
2) Claim 14 (presently amended)
Status: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 maintained (non-final).
Claim text on record (A1, GVNXDYBTPXXIFW1):
"A personal reminder digital voice recorder comprising: a) a battery operated audio microchip system for recording, storing and reproducing a single personal audio recording on each of a plurality of channels; b) a single playback button which can operate each of the plurality of channels; c) an a sing le LED corresponding to each of the channels, each LED having a means to turn the LED on when the channel has an active message recorded; and d) a means to turn each LED off when a corresponding channel has a message that is inactive." (entered as the currently amended claim)
Examiner's reasoning: The prior Office action (GQO3GTZ0PPOPPY5, dated 2011-08-01) relied on the Multi Message Recorder (MMR) product literature (as cited) to show a personal multi-channel voice recorder with per-channel stored messages and per-channel LED indication, and relied on Pawlowski (US 6,038,199) to show user interfaces that select among multiple stored voice files and play selected files using common playback controls. The combination of these teachings provides the elements recited in amended claim 14: the MMR teaching supplies the multiple channels, per-channel LEDs and LED behavior, while Pawlowski supplies the teaching of selecting stored messages for playback using a single playback control, thereby rendering a device with "a single playback button which can operate each of the plurality of channels" obvious for the stated purpose of reducing interface complexity while maintaining channel indication and playback capability. The earlier Office action specifically stated the ground for combining these teachings (GQO3GTZ0PPOPPY5: "Claim 14 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over 'MMR' ... in view of Pawlowski et al. ('199).").
Applicant's argument and Examiner response: Applicant argues that the references do not teach or suggest "a single playback button with multiple LEDs" and that if such a combination were obvious it would have been either stated or manufactured. The Examiner has considered the argument but finds it unpersuasive. The combination is reasoned: MMR teaches per-channel message storage and channel-specific LED indicators; Pawlowski teaches selection among stored voice files and common playback controls. It would have been within the routine skill of a person having ordinary skill in the field to combine these features to produce a compact personal recorder that uses a single playback control to play any selected channel while retaining per-channel LEDs to indicate message status. Applicant has not submitted documentary evidence that the combination is technically infeasible, nor evidence that either reference teaches away from combining the single-playback-control selection feature with per-channel visual indicators. Therefore the 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection of claim 14 is maintained.
Formal objection to claim form
The amendment filed with the A1 (GVNXDYBTPXXIFW1) contains a typographical/formatting error in the claim text: the phrase "an a sing le LED" appears where the intended phrase appears to be "an LED" or "a single LED"/"an LED corresponding to each of the channels". This typographical defect renders the claim text unclear and must be corrected. The applicant is required to submit a clean corrected claim in which the typographical error is fixed (e.g., "an LED corresponding to each of the channels"), under 37 C.F.R. 1.121(b) (amendments to the specification and claims after filing) or by an appropriate cancellation/replacement of the claim language. If the applicant chooses to submit a corrected claim, please also ensure that the corrected claim text is consistent with the intended scope as argued in the Remarks. The correction is a formality — once corrected, prosecution on the merits will continue with the maintained 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection unless applicant provides persuasive substantive rebuttal or submits further claim amendments to distinguish over the applied prior art.
Drawings
Corrected replacement drawings were submitted on 2011-12-13 (GW5F0MGKPXXIFW3). The drawing objections identified in the August 1, 2011 action are considered addressed by the replacement sheet and are withdrawn.
What the applicant can do next
- To overcome the maintained 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection of claim 14, applicant may: (1) submit an amendment to claim 14 that adds limitations not suggested by the applied references and which distinguish over the combination of MMR and Pawlowski (with explanation), or (2) submit persuasive arguments explaining why the combination of MMR and Pawlowski would not render the claimed subject matter obvious — for example, by pointing to specific passages in the cited references that teach away from the combination or by presenting evidence of unexpected results, teaching away, or other objective indicia of nonobviousness.
- Applicant must also correct the typographical/formatting error in the claim text (e.g., amend the phrase "an a sing le LED" to the intended phrase) so that the claim is clear and in proper form; submit the corrected claim language as an amendment under 37 C.F.R. 1.121(b). If applicant files such a correction, include an explanation if the correction changes claim scope in any way — otherwise indicate that the correction is a nonsubstantive typographical correction.
- If applicant chooses to further amend claim 14, please explain how the amendment changes patentability with respect to the cited references (MMR and Pawlowski).
Decision
The pending rejection of claim 14 under 35 U.S.C. 103 is maintained. Claims 1–13 are cancelled by applicant and are no longer before the Office. The drawing objections from the August 1, 2011 Office action are withdrawn based on the replacement drawings filed December 13, 2011 (GW5F0MGKPXXIFW3). Applicant must correct the typographical defect in the amended claim text and may then either respond with substantive arguments/evidence or propose further claim amendments to address the maintained rejection.
Sincerely,
Examining Corps (Art Unit 2614)
(Technical analysis and citations are based on the record in the application file, including GQO3GTZ0PPOPPY5 and the applicant submissions.)

No applicant evidence (e.g., affidavits, declarations, comparative test data) was supplied in the record to rebut the Examiner's prima facie obviousness combination; absent such evidence, the Examiner maintains the 103 rejection for claim 14.

1) Submit a clear, full claim set in which each claim is presented in full and is expressly identified as replacing the prior claims, with a request for entry under 37 C.F.R. § 1.121; or confirm and correct the facsimile-submitted claims so they may be entered as the official claims. 2) If the applicant prefers to keep the existing claim text (as examined 06/09/2008), file substantive arguments directed to the specific limitations that the examiner relied upon in applying Aihara and Ogishi, referencing specific passages of the prior art, so the examiner can respond on the merits.
